stone_theorem_costing.title: Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups
stone_theorem_costing.rationale: Discrete quantum systems evolve via unitary step operators without needing continuous time parameterizations. Stone's theorem U(t) = exp(-iHt) requires the continuum R and strong continuity; in finite discrete QM it functions as an external continuum interface with non-unique branch choices rather than an internal algebraic theorem.

historical_payload.terminal_statement: Discrete dynamics proceed by exact unitary steps over cyclotomic fields without continuous time or continuous generators. Stone's theorem is an imported continuum interface with countable branch ambiguity, not an internal consequence of finite quantum transitions.
